title: A vLLM flag took Kimi tool calls from 92 percent schema-valid to 100
friendlyTitle: A server setting made Kimi tool calls match the expected format every time
summary: Ubicloud says that serving Kimi K2.6 on vLLM 0.28 produced a valid tool-call schema only 92 percent of the time, so about 2 calls in 25 failed before the agent could run them. vLLM 0.31 added constrained decoding, off by default, behind a server flag. With it on, Ubicloud reports 100 percent schema accuracy on the Kimi and DeepSeek models it serves.
friendlySummary: Ubicloud says that serving Kimi K2.6 on vLLM version 0.28 produced a valid tool-call format only 92 percent of the time. About 2 calls in 25 failed before the agent could run them. vLLM 0.31 added a way to force the format, turned off by default, behind a server flag. With that flag on, Ubicloud reports a valid format 100 percent of the time on the Kimi and DeepSeek models it serves.
whyItMatters: If an open model looks worse in your agent than on a benchmark, the server may be the missing piece. vLLM left the strict mode off because turning it on by default caused problems for other models, including gpt-oss-20b, Qwen 3.6, and GLM 5.1. The practical check is narrow: if you serve Kimi or DeepSeek and tool calls are coming back malformed, the flag is the first thing to measure. A valid schema is not a correct action. It is the difference between a call the harness can run and one it has to throw away.
